product.schneider-towerat202.summary: The Tower AT with two floppy drives for working without a hard disk.
product.schneider-towerat202.history: Tower AT 202 occupied the dual-floppy tier between the basic 201 and hard-disk-equipped 220. Schneider included it in the same service manual as both, within the range documented in 1988. It retained the compact case and separate CPU card; a second drive made it easier to alternate programs and data on floppies.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.c: The commercial difference lies in the drives. The 202 configuration is described with two 3.5-inch 720 KB floppy drives; no specific launch price has been confirmed in the preserved sources.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.f: No pair is specifically identified as a 202 dump. The preserved sets belong to Tower AT 2xx; sharing a manual with the 201 and 220 does not establish interchangeability across all revisions.
product.schneider-towerat202.warning: Historical sheet under research; booting in BluMach remains unvalidated.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.v: Sources and file hashes have been checked. BluMach a1b0125d has no dedicated entry for this model; MAME groups Tower AT 2xx machines as not working. Booting has not been tested.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.l: The complete machine still needs validation. Board, BIOS pair and video ROM must be identified, then POST, memory, keyboard, RTC, disks and ports tested before usable emulation can be claimed.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.b: The CPU and memory occupy a separate card. The 201/202/220 manual documents Tower CPU286 50229, GC101/GC102 logic, DS1287 RTC and 8042/8742 keyboard controller; it includes different circuit revisions.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.m: Expansion depends on the installed board. The manual diagram shows a 512 KB base and optional DIL/SIMM banks; it does not prove that every unit has the connectors fitted.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.v: Integrated video leaves expansion slots available. The 1988 review documents EGA and up to 800 × 600 with a multisync monitor and suitable software; it counts three 16-bit slots and one 8-bit slot.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.m: Schneider, Service Manual Tower AT 201/202/220, Ident-Nr. 44657, 03/1989: cover and CPU/memory diagrams reviewed; PDF preserved.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.r: Happy Computer 11/1988, M. Ohnesorg/rz, Rechengiganten zu Niedrigpreisen, pp. 97–98 and 101: review of a Tower AT without a hard disk, with no commercial suffix identified.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.m: Happy Computer 05/1989, Sammlerstück, p. 18: 220 Mega edition, equipment, prices and announced production run; scan and transcription preserved.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.r: Jungsi, Schneider VGA AT System 40: range overview and approximate chronology; not a substitute for a manual covering each revision.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.m: MAME, at.cpp: towerat2xx sets, variant provenance and unresolved EGA pairings. Files are preserved in the library; their presence does not prove universal compatibility.
product.schneider-towerat202.technical.c: BluMach a1b0125d, inspected and preserved machine table: no dedicated Tower AT entry.
